approachQuestion.prompt: A label cleaner receives an immutable string of n lowercase English letters, 0 <= n <= 200,000. Repeatedly delete the leftmost adjacent pair of equal letters until no such pair remains. Return the remaining string in order; the empty string is allowed. Choose a method minimizing worst-case total time. Input: "azxxza". Output: "", because deleting xx exposes zz, whose deletion exposes aa. Input: "abca". Output: "abca".

options.text: Scan letters left to right with a stack. If the next letter equals the top, pop it; otherwise push it. Copy the remaining bottom-to-top letters into the result.
options.feedback: The stack is the fully reduced prefix. Only its final letter can form a new adjacent pair with the next input letter.

options.text: Mark pairs adjacent in the original input, delete those marked letters, and return without checking newly exposed neighbors.
options.feedback: For azxxza, deleting only the original xx leaves azza, but more cancellations are required.

options.text: Count each letter and output one copy of each letter with an odd count, in alphabetical order.
options.feedback: abca remains abca under adjacent deletion; counts would instead produce bc and lose order and adjacency.

options.text: Copy the string to a mutable array. Find and delete its leftmost equal adjacent pair, shift the suffix, and restart the search until no pair remains.
options.feedback: This implements the specified deletion order, but repeatedly scans and shifts prefixes and suffixes that a reduced frontier would retain.

feedback.reason: New cancellations occur at the boundary between the reduced prefix and the next letter.
details: Keep the reduced prefix in an array stack. Cancel a matching top with the incoming letter, or append that letter. Finally copy the live prefix into the output string.

The stack is the fully reduced processed prefix. Removing a matching pair may expose a new matching boundary, so keep processing against the current top. A returned string copy does not exclude the separate reduction buffer.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For retain-reduced-prefix, choose the tightest worst-case total time and auxiliary-space bounds in terms of n, the input length.
constraints: The input is immutable and excluded from auxiliary space. Returned output is excluded, but all working buffers count even if later copied into output.
Fixed-size integers, characters, indices and comparisons take constant time. Arithmetic is unit cost under the stated range guarantee.
Use an iterative implementation with a preallocated n-entry array and a top index: push and pop take constant time. No recursion, hashing, or hidden whole-buffer copies occur.
Materializing output takes time proportional to its length; no persistent snapshots or string concatenation are used.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each character is pushed and popped at most once before final copying.
details: Each character is pushed at most once and popped at most once; copying the final string is also linear. An alternating input retains n characters in the working buffer, so auxiliary space is O(n) even though the returned copy is excluded.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: An alternating string causes no cancellation and leaves n characters in the separate reduction buffer, outside returned output.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each incoming letter is pushed once or cancels one earlier top; total cancellations cannot exceed prior pushes.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A final letter can alter the reduced suffix, so deciding the complete result can require scanning the full string.
